etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English, from Old French noble, from Latin nōbilis (“knowable, known, well-known, famous, celebrated, high-born, of noble birth, excellent”), from nōscere, gnōscere (“to know”).

False cognate of Arabic نبيل (nabīl). Displaced native Middle English athel, from Old English æþele.

definitions.definition: An aristocrat; one of aristocratic blood. [from 14th c.]
(historical) A medieval gold coin of England in the 14th and 15th centuries, usually valued at 6s 8d. [from 14th c.]

quote.citation: 1499, John Skelton, The Bowge of Courte:
quote.text: I lyked no thynge his playe, / For yf I had not quyckely fledde the touche, / He had plucte oute the nobles of my pouche.
And who shall then stick closest to ye, and excite others? not he who takes up armes for cote and conduct, and his four nobles of Danegelt.

quote.citation: 2011, Thomas Penn, Winter King, Penguin, published 2012, page 93:
quote.text: There, before the high altar, as the choir's voices soared upwards to the blue, star-flecked ceiling, Henry knelt and made his offering of a ‘noble in gold’, 6s 8d.

definitions.definition: Having honorable qualities; having moral eminence and freedom from anything petty, mean or dubious in conduct and character.

quote.citation: 1997, 1:44:10 from the start, in The Fifth Element‎[1] (Science Fiction / Action), →ISBN, →OCLC:
quote.text: Korben, I realize you must be pretty mad at me. But I want you to know that I am fighting for a noble cause. / Yes, you're trying to save the world. I remember.

quote.citation: 1918, W[illiam] B[abington] Maxwell, chapter V, in The Mirror and the Lamp, Indianapolis, Ind.: The Bobbs-Merrill Company, →OCLC:
quote.text: He was thinking; but the glory of the song, the swell from the great organ, the clustered lights,  […] , the height and vastness of this noble fane, its antiquity and its strength—all these things seemed to have their part as causes of the thrilling emotion that accompanied his thoughts.

definitions.definition: Of exalted rank; of or relating to the nobility; distinguished from the masses by birth, station, or title; highborn.

(winemaking) Belonging to a class of grape cultivars traditionally considered most favorable for winemaking, usually encompassing the six: Merlot, Pinot Noir,  Cabernet Sauvignon,  Sauvignon blanc,  Chardonnay, and Riesling.
(geometry, of a polyhedron) Both isohedral and isogonal.
